# trashwheelexplorer

An R package with a Shiny app for exploring what Baltimore’s Trash
Wheels collect.

**Documentation website:**
<https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-kjam0022/>

## Purpose

**Intended user:** an analyst at a Baltimore waterway-cleanup programme
who needs to decide which kinds of rubbish to target.

**Question:** Which types of rubbish does each Trash Wheel collect most
per dumpster load, and has that changed over the years?

The app lets the analyst choose Trash Wheels, rubbish types and a range
of years. It then shows how the average number of items per dumpster
load changes over time, which wheel is highest for each rubbish type,
and the numbers behind the chart.

## Data

The package includes `trash_collections`, a data frame of dumpster
collections from four Trash Wheels (Mister, Professor, Captain and
Gwynnda) between 2014 and 2023. It has 6,951 rows: 993 dumpster
collections, each with seven rubbish types. Item counts are estimates
based on samples. A missing count means the rubbish type was not
recorded, not that nothing was collected, so the package never treats
missing counts as zero.

- **Source:** TidyTuesday, Trash Wheel Collection Data (2024-03-05),
  <https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2024/2024-03-05>.
- **Original data:** Mr. Trash Wheel Baltimore Healthy Harbor
  initiative, <https://www.mrtrashwheel.com/>.
- **Preparation:** `data-raw/trash_collections.R` downloads the CSV,
  cleans the names, parses the dates and reshapes the data from wide to
  long. Run it to rebuild `data/trash_collections.rda`.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-kjam0022")
```

## Launch the app

``` r

library(trashwheelexplorer)
run_app()
```

## Use the summary function

[`summarise_trash()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-kjam0022/reference/summarise_trash.md)
summarises the average and total items per collection by wheel, year and
rubbish type:

``` r

library(trashwheelexplorer)

summarise_trash(
  trash_collections,
  wheels = "Mister Trash Wheel",
  trash_types = "Plastic Bottles",
  years = c(2020, 2023)
)
```
